# Notice: licenses and attribution of the bundled datasets

<!-- Generated by `python -m scripts.generate` from the dataset information in pyml_datasets/datasets/. Do not edit it by hand. -->

The code of pyml-datasets is released under the MIT license, see `LICENSE`. The datasets were created by other people. Each one is redistributed under the license it has at its source, and the changes made to it are listed here, as these licenses require. The license texts are in the `LICENSES` folder.

## Abalone (`abalone`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Warwick Nash, Tracy Sellers, Simon Talbot, Andrew Cawthorn, Wes Ford
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/1/abalone)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 1, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 4177 examples with 8 inputs. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Nash, W., Sellers, T., Talbot, S., Cawthorn, A., & Ford, W. (1994). Abalone [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C55C7W
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Features and the target are stored as float64.
  - The column Sex is stored as integer codes, in the order of the category names listed for it. The names of the columns are written in lower case, for example Whole_weight is stored as whole_weight. The target is the number of rings.
  - The continuous values are stored as the source gives them, with the scaling that the notes describe.
- **Notes:**
  - The source says that examples with missing values were removed from the original data, most of them because the number of rings was missing, and that the ranges of the continuous values were scaled for use with an artificial neural network by dividing by 200. Keep this in mind when you use the units mm and grams that the variable table of UCI lists.
  - The data comes from a study that was not made for machine learning, by the Marine Resources Division of the Department of Primary Industry and Fisheries, Tasmania. The dataset was donated to UCI by Sam Waugh of the University of Tasmania.
  - The sex is M, F or I (infant).
  - The number of rings plus 1.5 gives the age of the abalone in years.

## Adult (`adult`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Barry Becker, Ronny Kohavi
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/2/adult)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 2, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 48842 examples with 14 inputs, the training part of the source (adult.data, 32561 rows) followed by its test part (adult.test, 16281 rows). The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Becker, B. & Kohavi, R. (1996). Adult [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5XW20
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Numeric features are stored as float64 and the target as int64 labels.
  - Categorical features are stored as integer codes, in the order of the category names listed for each feature. The categories are in alphabetical order, except those of education, which are in the order of the education level, so its code is education_num minus one. The target is 0 for <=50K and 1 for >50K.
  - The training part and the test part of the source are stored together, the training part first. The test part writes the target with a trailing dot (<=50K. and >50K.). The dot is dropped, so both parts use the same two classes.
  - Entries of workclass, occupation and native_country that the source marks as missing are stored as NaN. UCI delivers some of them as the text ? and some as empty cells, both become NaN.
  - The hyphens in the column names are replaced with underscores, for example marital-status becomes marital_status.
- **Notes:**
  - Missing entries, the text ? in the source, occur in workclass, occupation and native_country: 6465 values in 3620 rows, which leaves 45222 complete rows, the number that the source documentation gives. The missing entries are NaN, so fill or drop them before fitting a model that cannot handle NaN.
  - The first 32561 rows are the training part of the source and the last 16281 rows are its test part, so slicing the rows gives back the split of the source.
  - The classes are not balanced: 11687 of the 48842 people, 23.93 percent, are in the class above 50K, as the source documentation states.
  - education_num is the education level as a number. It holds the same information as education, because every education has exactly one education_num in the source.
  - Rows that repeat an earlier row are kept as they are in the source.
  - race and sex are features of the dataset, and the UCI variables table marks them as demographic variables. A model that uses them can reproduce social bias, so check its fairness before it is used for decisions about people.

## Airfoil Self-Noise (`airfoil_self_noise`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Thomas Brooks, D. Pope, Michael Marcolini
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/291/airfoil+self+noise)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 291, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 1503 examples with 5 inputs. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Brooks, T., Pope, D., & Marcolini, M. (1989). Airfoil Self-Noise [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5VW2C.
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Features and the target are stored as float64.
  - The columns are named after their descriptions in the variables table of the source, written in lower case with underscores: attack-angle is stored as angle_of_attack, chord-length as chord_length, free-stream-velocity as free_stream_velocity, suction-side-displacement-thickness as suction_side_displacement_thickness, and the target scaled-sound-pressure as scaled_sound_pressure_level. frequency keeps its name. The features are stored in the order of the variables table.
- **Notes:**
  - The NASA data set comprises different size NACA 0012 airfoils at various wind tunnel speeds and angles of attack. The span of the airfoil and the observer position were the same in all of the experiments.
  - Units: the frequency is in Hz, the angle of attack in degrees, the chord length in meters, the free-stream velocity in meters per second, the suction side displacement thickness in meters and the scaled sound pressure level in decibels.
  - In the data file of the source the frequency takes whole numbers from 200 to 20000 (21 different values), the angle of attack takes 27 different values from 0 to 22.2, the chord length takes 6 different values from 0.0254 to 0.3048 and the free-stream velocity takes 4 different values: 31.7, 39.6, 55.5 and 71.3.
  - The variables table of UCI lists the angle of attack as binary, but the data file has 27 different values for it, as written above. It is stored as the number the source gives.

## Auto MPG (`auto_mpg`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** R. Quinlan
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/9/auto+mpg)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 9, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 398 examples of the revised version, in which the source already removed 8 examples of the StatLib original because their mpg was unknown. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Quinlan, R. (1993). Auto MPG [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5859H
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Features and the target mpg are stored as float64.
  - The 6 missing values of horsepower are stored as NaN.
  - The column car_name, which UCI marks as an identifier and describes as a string that is unique for each instance, is not stored, because X holds numbers only. The other columns are stored in the order of the data description of the source.
- **Notes:**
  - The source took the data from the StatLib library at Carnegie Mellon University, where it was used in the 1983 American Statistical Association Exposition, and calls it a slightly modified version of that dataset.
  - 6 values of horsepower are missing and stored as NaN. Impute them or drop the rows before fitting a model that cannot handle NaN.
  - cylinders, model_year and origin are multi-valued discrete features in the source and are stored as its numbers. The source does not say what the numbers of origin stand for, so origin has no category names.
  - mpg is fuel consumption in miles per gallon, so a higher value means a more economical car.

## Bank Marketing (`bank_marketing`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** S. Moro, P. Rita, P. Cortez
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/222/bank+marketing)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 222, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 45211 examples with 16 inputs (the bank-full version). The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Moro, S., Rita, P., & Cortez, P. (2014). Bank Marketing [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5K306
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Numeric features are stored as float64 and the target as int64 labels.
  - Categorical features are stored as integer codes, in the order of the category names listed for each feature. The target is 0 for no and 1 for yes.
  - Entries of job, education, contact and poutcome that the UCI release marks as missing are stored as the category unknown, which the data description of the source lists for these features. No NaN values are stored.
  - The column that UCI calls day_of_week is named day, because the source describes it as the day of the month of the last contact.
- **Notes:**
  - The duration of the last call is only known after the call, and the call ends with the answer. The source advises to use duration for benchmarks only and to drop it for a realistic predictive model.
  - pdays is -1 for clients who were not contacted in a previous campaign. The value is kept as it is in the source.
  - The classes are not balanced: far fewer clients subscribed than not.

## Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) (`breast_cancer`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** William Wolberg, Olvi Mangasarian, Nick Street, W. Street
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/17/breast+cancer+wisconsin+diagnostic)
- **Obtained from:** scikit-learn (sklearn.datasets.load_breast_cancer), which redistributes a copy of the data. The scikit-learn version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Wolberg, W., Mangasarian, O., Street, N., & Street, W. (1993). Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5DW2B
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Values are stored as float64 and the diagnosis as int64 labels (0 = malignant, 1 = benign).
  - The diagnosis is a number instead of the letters used in the UCI file, and the sample identifier column is not included.
  - Feature and class names follow scikit-learn.
- **Notes:**
  - This dataset is for learning about machine learning methods. It is not a medical tool and must not be used to diagnose anything.

## Combined Cycle Power Plant (`combined_cycle_power_plant`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Pınar Tüfekci, Heysem Kaya
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/294/combined+cycle+power+plant)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 294, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 9568 examples with 4 inputs. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Tfekci, P. & Kaya, H. (2014). Combined Cycle Power Plant [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5002N.
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Features and the target are stored as float64.
  - The columns are named after their descriptions in the variables table of the source, written in lower case with underscores: AT is stored as temperature, V as exhaust_vacuum, AP as ambient_pressure, RH as relative_humidity and the target PE as net_hourly_electrical_energy_output. The features are stored in the order AT, V, AP, RH.
- **Notes:**
  - The features are hourly averages of ambient variables. The averages are taken from various sensors located around the plant that record the variables every second. The source gives the variables without normalization.
  - Units: the temperature is in degrees Celsius, the exhaust vacuum in cm Hg, the ambient pressure in millibar, the relative humidity in percent and the net hourly electrical energy output in MW. The source documents the ranges 1.81 to 37.11 for the temperature, 25.36 to 81.56 for the exhaust vacuum, 992.89 to 1033.30 for the ambient pressure, 25.56 to 100.16 for the relative humidity and 420.26 to 495.76 for the output. The relative humidity goes above 100 percent in the source and is stored as it is.
  - According to the source the exhaust vacuum is collected from and has an effect on the steam turbine, and the other three variables affect the performance of the gas turbine.
  - To allow 5x2 fold statistical tests, the source provides the data shuffled five times. This dataset holds the rows in the order of the table that UCI serves through ucimlrepo.
  - UCI prints the citation, and the name of the first creator on its page, without the letters of the name Tüfekci that are not in the English alphabet. The citation is given here as UCI prints it, the name of the creator as it is written in the papers of the source.

## Concrete Compressive Strength (`concrete_strength`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** I-Cheng Yeh
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/165/concrete+compressive+strength)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 165, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 1030 examples with 8 inputs. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Yeh, I. (1998). Concrete Compressive Strength [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5PK67
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Features and the target are stored as float64.
  - The names of the columns are written in lower case with underscores, for example Blast Furnace Slag is stored as blast_furnace_slag. The features are stored in the order of the data description of the source, the target is the concrete compressive strength.
- **Notes:**
  - The seven ingredients are given in kg in a m3 mixture, the age in days (1 to 365) and the compressive strength in MPa.
  - The source describes the compressive strength of concrete as a highly nonlinear function of age and ingredients.
  - The data file that UCI offers for download (Concrete_Data.xls) has more decimals than the table that ucimlrepo returns and that is stored here: the amounts of the ingredients differ by at most 0.05 and the strength by less than 0.005.

## Default of Credit Card Clients (`credit_card_default`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** I-Cheng Yeh
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/350/default+of+credit+card+clients)
- **Obtained from:** UCI dataset 350, read with the ucimlrepo package (version stored in extras['ucimlrepo_version']).
- **Citation:** Yeh, I. (2009). Default of Credit Card Clients [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C55S3H.
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format.
  - The row identifier column ID of the source is not included.
  - Column names X1..X23 were replaced with the feature names from the UCI variable descriptions; the values themselves were not modified.
  - Features were converted to float64.
  - Target Y was kept as integer 0/1 codes, and the class names were set from the Yes/No meaning in the source description.
- **Notes:**
  - SEX uses the codes 1 (male) and 2 (female) as documented by the source, so the category codes do not start at 0.
  - EDUCATION is documented as 1 = graduate school, 2 = university, 3 = high school, 4 = others. The data also contains the undocumented values 0, 5 and 6.
  - MARRIAGE is documented as 1 = married, 2 = single, 3 = others. The data also contains the undocumented value 0.
  - The repayment status columns PAY_0, PAY_2, PAY_3, PAY_4, PAY_5 and PAY_6 are documented with the scale -1 = pay duly, 1 to 9 = payment delay in months. The data also contains the undocumented values -2 and 0 in all six columns, and the value 9 does not occur. The value 1 does not occur in PAY_5 and PAY_6. There is no column PAY_1: PAY_0 is the repayment status of September 2005, as in the source.
  - All raw values are kept as they are in the source; no recoding, cleaning or removal of rows was applied.

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** E. Alpaydin, C. Kaynak

## Energy Efficiency (`energy_efficiency`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Athanasios Tsanas, Angeliki Xifara
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/242/energy+efficiency)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 242, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 768 examples with 8 inputs and 2 targets. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Tsanas, A. & Xifara, A. (2012). Energy Efficiency [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C51307.
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Features and targets are stored as float64.
  - The two targets are stored together: y has the shape (768, 2), the first column is the heating load (Y1 of the source) and the second column is the cooling load (Y2).
  - The columns X1 to X8 are named after their descriptions in the variables table of the source, written in lower case with underscores, for example Glazing Area Distribution (X8) is stored as glazing_area_distribution. The features are stored in the order X1 to X8.
- **Notes:**
  - The buildings are 12 different building shapes simulated in Ecotect. They differ in the glazing area, the distribution of the glazing area and the orientation, among other parameters, and 768 building shapes were obtained by simulating various settings of these characteristics.
  - The source says the aim is to predict each of the two responses from the eight features, and that the data can also be used as a multi-class classification problem if the response is rounded to the nearest integer. This library stores it as a regression dataset.
  - orientation and glazing_area_distribution are integers in the source. The source does not say what their numbers stand for, so they are stored as its numbers without category names.
  - The source does not state the units of the columns, so none are given here.

## Forest Fires (`forest_fires`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Paulo Cortez, Anbal Morais
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/162/forest+fires)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 162, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 517 examples with 12 inputs and the target area. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Cortez, P. & Morais, A. (2007). Forest Fires [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5D88D
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. The features and the target are stored as float64.
  - The categorical features month and day are stored as integer codes, in the order of the category names listed for each feature: the months from jan to dec and the days of the week from mon to sun.
- **Notes:**
  - The target area is very skewed towards 0.0. The source page says that it may make sense to model it with the logarithm transform, and the paper of the source used ln(x+1). The values are stored as released, without any transform.
  - X and Y are the coordinates of a grid on the map of the Montesinho park, stored as whole numbers.
  - The variables table of UCI lists DMC, rain and area as integers, although the ranges that it gives for them have decimals. The values are stored as real numbers.

## German Credit (`german_credit`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Hans Hofmann
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/144/statlog+german+credit+data)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 144, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: the original categorical/symbolic form of the data (the file german.data), all 1000 examples with 20 attributes. The numeric version of the source (german.data-numeric) is not used. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Hofmann, H. (1994). Statlog (German Credit Data) [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5NC77
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Numeric features are stored as float64 and the target as int64 labels.
  - Categorical features are stored as integer codes, in the order of the category names listed for each feature. Every category name starts with the code of the source (for example A11), followed by the meaning that the source gives to the code.
  - The attributes, which the source calls Attribute1 to Attribute20, have descriptive names taken from the data description of the source, in the order of the source.
  - The target is 0 for a good and 1 for a bad credit risk. The source codes them as 1 and 2, in the same order.
- **Notes:**
  - The source requires a cost matrix. Its rows are the actual class and its columns the predicted class, and a correct decision costs 0. Classifying a bad customer as good costs 5 and classifying a good customer as bad costs 1. With the classes of this file (0 good, 1 bad) the matrix is [[0, 1], [5, 0]]. The matrix is not stored in the file, so a user has to apply it.
  - The classes are not balanced: 700 good and 300 bad credit risks.
  - The integer codes of a categorical feature are labels, not quantities. Some features are ordered (for example savings), but the codes are not distances, and unordered features such as purpose have no order at all.
  - The source lists the category A47 of purpose and the category A95 of personal_status_sex, but neither occurs in the 1000 samples. They stay in the lists of categories, so the codes keep the order of the source.
  - personal_status_sex mixes the sex and the marital status of the applicant, and age and foreign_worker describe the applicant as a person. Use these attributes with care: a model that decides about real people on such grounds can be unfair.

## Palmer Penguins (`penguins`)

- **License:** [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)
- **Creators:** Allison Marie Horst, Alison Presmanes Hill, Kristen B Gorman
- **Source:** [palmerpenguins data package (Palmer Station Antarctica LTER and K. Gorman)](https://github.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/tree/v0.1.0)
- **Obtained from:** The file inst/extdata/penguins.csv of the GitHub repository allisonhorst/palmerpenguins, tag v0.1.0. Its SHA-256 digest is pinned in the build recipe.
- **Citation:** Horst AM, Hill AP, Gorman KB (2020). palmerpenguins: Palmer Archipelago (Antarctica) penguin data. R package version 0.1.0. https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/. doi:10.5281/zenodo.3960218.
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Measurements are stored as float64 and the species as int64 labels (0 = Adelie, 1 = Chinstrap, 2 = Gentoo).
  - The columns island and sex are stored as integer codes, see the categorical features. The missing values (NA in the CSV file) are stored as NaN.

## Real Estate Valuation (`real_estate_valuation`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** I-Cheng Yeh
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/477/real+estate+valuation+data+set)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 477, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package: all 414 examples with 6 inputs and the target. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Yeh, I. (2018). Real Estate Valuation [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5J30W
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. The features and the target are stored as float64.
  - The identifier column No, the numbers 1 to 414, is not stored, because it is not a feature.
  - The column names are written in lowercase with underscores, and the prefixes X1 to X6 and Y are dropped, for example X3 distance to the nearest MRT station becomes distance_to_nearest_mrt_station.
- **Notes:**
  - The source says that the data set was randomly split into a training part (2/3 of the samples) and a testing part (1/3), but its file has no column that tells which sample belongs to which part. All 414 samples are stored and the split is not provided.
  - The transaction date is a number: 2013.250 is March 2013 and 2013.500 is June 2013, as the source describes. Only 12 different dates occur, from 2012.667 to 2013.583. ucimlrepo gives the dates rounded to three decimals, while the xlsx file of the UCI page has seven (the first sale: 2012.9166667), so the stored dates differ from that file by 0.0004 at most.
  - The target is the house price of unit area in 10000 New Taiwan Dollar per Ping, where a Ping is a local unit of area, 1 Ping = 3.3 square meters, as the source gives.

## Wine Quality (`wine_quality`)

- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Creators:** Paulo Cortez, A. Cerdeira, F. Almeida, T. Matos, J. Reis
- **Source:** [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/186/wine+quality)
- **Obtained from:** UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 186, downloaded with the ucimlrepo package. The ucimlrepo version is recorded in the file.
- **Citation:** Cortez, P., Cerdeira, A., Almeida, F., Matos, T., & Reis, J. (2009). Wine Quality [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C56S3T
- **Changes made:**
  - Converted to the NumPy NPZ format. Features and the quality score are stored as float64.
  - The red wines (1599) and the white wines (4898) are stored together. As in the UCI release, the colour of the wine is not a feature.
